September 2026 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30), all shifts. Window coverage: complete.
Contribution margin not set: without an owner margin no lost contribution is priced, so the dollars are paper and machine time.
The ownership lens: the total cost of the waste recorded, side trim first, then the rest by dollars, each line of the waste breakdown priced once, so the total is the waste breakdown's.
A banded line is split at its band: at standard, the cost of the order mix and the process; above standard, the lever's own figure.
The dry-end waste is the tag scrap: bond, warp, misalignment, moisture and other, one subtotal with each kind beneath it.

A yearly figure is this period's rate, period-to-date dollars per production day x the post's production days a year; for all shifts it is each shift's period-to-date rate added up, so the shifts' yearly figures add to it.

Whole dollars that add up: each shift of each production day prints its nearest dollar, its lines sharing it by the largest remainder, and every day, window and line is its shifts' whole dollars added up.

Over several days these whole dollars, added shift by shift, can read off the same quantities priced at once in cents, which the formulas and receipts state; over the whole record the widest gap measured is about twenty-five dollars, on a month's waste recorded.
How a dollar is priced, for Side trim (all recorded): 5,677,925.3 sq ft = 5,677.925 MSF x $55/MSF paper = $312,285.89; contribution: margin not set. It prints $312,288 (whole dollars that add up).

Rates: paper $55/MSF (post), machine time $1,200/hr (post), contribution margin not set (assumption: owner to set), trim target 3% (owner, 2026-11-10). Dollars are synthetic records priced at assumed rates (the post's defaults unless changed); they are not a real plant's figures.
Where to look
- The weekly trend of trim → “Trend of trim over eight weeks”
- Side trim, shear and each dry-end reason → “Waste breakdown this month”
- Volume, speed and waste by grade → “Volume by grade this month”
